data.body:
=== HANDOFF #5 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ AFTER #4. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam @ 3 commits above 8ffdcea0d.
ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

THREE CORRECTIONS TO HANDOFF #4 — it said 8c35 and bda8 were "ready to CLOSE". NEITHER WAS.

 1. bda8's close returned SEVEN unmet criteria. Six were genuinely missing work, now implemented and
    pushed (change 1113): the construction-time conformance guard did not exist at all — the port
    declared the members and NOTHING checked them where a backend is built, so `isinstance` returning
    False in a test was a demonstration that a guard was possible, not a guard. Added
    `assert_transport_conforms()` and wired it into BOTH factories (Cloud too: the port states what
    the CORE requires). Verified both real transports satisfy it BEFORE relying on it, so the guard
    cannot make a shipped backend unbuildable — that check is itself now a test. Plus four tests:
    reporter idempotence via the real `_identity_of`, `set_entity_property` key/value integrity, a
    `caplog` assertion that the WARNING actually FIRES, and `validate_assignee_exists` raising
    `AssigneeNotFoundError` specifically. ALL FOUR MUTATION-CHECKED (removing each guard call,
    blanking `logger.warning`, deleting `_diff_reporter`'s early return -> exactly the expected
    failures).
    The 7th criterion ("`git diff` shows test_reconcile_pass.py unchanged") was UNMEETABLE: that
    file's writing-mode assertions called `_envelope()`, and `__main__.py:444-452` shows only the
    `no_write` branch emits JSON — the assertion could never have passed and was masked by the
    crash-on-missing-member. The operator authorised remediating it; it is now three verifiable
    properties (no assertion deleted without a still-failing replacement; envelope-emitting modes
    keep their assertions; every change cites the emitting code) instead of a git-diff invariant.

 2. 8c35's close returned one unmet criterion, correctly: the guide's commands had NEVER been run.
    Change 1115 adds `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`, which PARSES the
    config block out of `docs/user-guide.md` at runtime — a restated copy would keep passing while
    the doc rotted. Writes a pyproject.toml, because `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` is the pyproject
    surface (`_config_sources.py:111-115`) while `rebar.toml` takes bare `[reconciler]`; the existing
    live module uses the OTHER form, so reusing its fixture would have proven the guide by not using
    it. Asserts a `no_write` envelope, the extra really exists, and that JIRA_PAT is env-only (PAT in
    config + absent from env MUST fail naming the variable — the guide sells that as a security
    property).

 3. PREFIX COLLISIONS. `f391` and `b586` each match TWO tickets. Use f391-806b-938f-45d8 (PAT cap)
    and b586-2fda-8a15-4260 (rate limiter).

f391 IS FIXED (change 1114). `jira_dc_pat` is session-scoped (O(1) tokens, not O(tests)) plus a
session-start sweep of leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` PATs. The sweep ONLY touches that prefix — the
admin account may hold a human's PATs and deleting one to reclaim budget would be worse than the bug;
that exclusion is a test with teeth (incl. a prefix-adjacent name that must NOT match). 13 unit tests
against a stubbed `_request`; the scope fix is mutation-checked.

NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FILED — [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd], THE THIRD SIBLING.
`fetcher._iter_pages` (fetcher.py:324-326) stops on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED size —
identical to the `get_parent_map` bug fixed in 1105. REPRODUCED, not inferred: a client serving 250
issues while capping pages at 20 yields 20. **92% of the inbound snapshot silently lost.** Worse than
9263: `collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so it loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES, and every unseen bound
issue becomes a candidate for the deletion path. NOT folded into 9263 deliberately — 9263 is
adapter-local, this is CORE on the shared Cloud path, so it needs its own review and its own proof
the Cloud contract (cap / ACLI ceiling / same-token-twice) is unchanged.

21fc's OWN REMEDIATION IS WRONG — corrected on the ticket, plan not yet rewritten.
There are TWO index-dependent sites, and 21fc names only the first:
  1. `recover_pending` keyless branch — unbinds on a negative search (the site 21fc describes);
  2. `create_one`'s JQL dedup (dispatch_one.py:237-238) — on a miss it CREATES. THIS is what writes
     the duplicate.
Fixing only site 1 does NOT help: `outbound_differ.py:528-531` gates the create on
`get_jira_key(local_id) is None`, and a keyless-pending entry HAS `jira_key: None`
(binding_store.py:258-262), so the create is emitted anyway and the dedup misses for the same
index-lag reason. `is_pending()` exists (binding_store.py:270) and the differ does not consult it.
THE FIX MUST BE AT THE CREATE GATE: defer the create while a keyless-pending binding is inside an
index-lag grace window. The AC must drive the WHOLE path (crash -> recover -> differ -> create) under
a lagging client and assert EXACTLY ONE issue created; a test asserting only "recover_pending did not
unbind" passes while the duplicate is still written.

J11 (5200) — ROUND 4 BLOCKED, 7 findings, ALL FIXED IN THE PLAN. And it produced a SEQUENCING result:
**5200 now depends_on deac, so J11 cannot be claimed until the pagination defects land** — the gate
agrees with the finding. The pagination AC ("seed 2*observed+1") is MEANINGLESS while 9263 and deac
stand: seeding past the page size would silently truncate and report a converged pass over a fraction
of the data — the exact green-but-broken outcome J11 exists to end.
Two findings corrected MY errors, both verified in source before accepting:
  * `prev_snapshot` is the OUTBOUND field-change baseline (`OutboundDiffConfig.prev_snapshot`), so a
    leftover production copy produces a wave of spurious outbound UPDATEs — NOT deletions. The AC now
    asserts zero deletions AND <10 outbound updates, because a deletion-only assertion passes at a
    reassuring zero while the run is corrupted in the way that actually happens. (This is the THIRD
    restatement of this file's role in the plan; it is now stated from the code path.)
  * `set_parent`'s NotImplementedError is SWALLOWED by `dispatch_one.py:564`, so asserting it through
    the reconciler subprocess is untestable by construction. It must be asserted directly against the
    transport.
  * the "no production Jira key reference" AC was MECHANICALLY UNACHIEVABLE — ticket event files
    legitimately embed `jira_key` from prior Cloud syncs and the scrub correctly leaves them. Replaced
    with `.bridge_state*` scrub completeness.
I ALSO RAN LESSON 4 (grep the whole document after editing) AND IT CAUGHT A REAL CONTRADICTION: the
Approach opener listed "pagination" among defects the store copy surfaces, while the volume bullet
says pagination is remote-side and the copy does not exercise it. Fixed. That habit works — use it.

REVISED ORDER (changed by the above): deac + 9263 FIRST (they gate J11's evidence), THEN J11, THEN
21fc (with the corrected two-site fix), 387d, 7c26, b586.

IN FLIGHT: changes 1113/1114/1115 awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. deac's plan review running.

ENVIRONMENT WARNINGS
 * ANOTHER AGENT SESSION runs concurrently in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam (ticket 7f86).
   It competes for CPU and for LLM gates and it pushes to main. The unit suite took 24 MINUTES under
   that contention. Expect it; do not diagnose it as a code problem.
 * DO NOT run a full `pytest tests/unit` while committing — 7 "Test moved the repo HEAD" ERRORS in
   this session were caused by my own commits landing mid-run, not by defects. Counts are not causes.
 * A test placed in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` WITHOUT a harness skipif does NOT run harness-free:
   the session-scoped autouse `_jira_dc_harness_ready` waits out the full 20-minute budget and then
   errors (measured 1208s), and `tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py` FAILS the build for it. Put
   repo-only checks in `tests/unit/`.
